newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. wants Iraq oil deal renewal kept at $2 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.N. wants Iraq oil deal renewal kept at $2 billion.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to recommend that the $2 billion oil-for-food deal for Iraq be renewed in June on the same terms as the present six-month plan, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.

The deal expires on June 7 and Annan is expected to give his recommendations by the end of the month to the Security Council, which must adopt another resolution. Key council members as well as Iraq probably have been or will be consulted in advance of his formal proposals, diplomats said.

The current accord allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months in order to purchase food, medicine and other goods for its people suffering under U.N. sanctions imposed when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
About two-thirds of the monies are for the humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
Iraq has complained frequently that the council's procedures had prevented the supplies from reaching the country within a reasonable period of time while oil sales moved quickly.

Its key negotiator for the scheme, Abdul Amir al-Anbari, based in Paris, said last month that Baghdad needed at least $4 billion in oil revenues to meet its needs. He also proposed that a week or two be allocated for settling the pending orders for humanitarian supplies.
"Iraq wants an expansion in sales, but an expansion would be extremely difficult," said the U.N. official, speaking on condition of anonymity.
According to the official, most governments supported an extension of the current arrangements.

He said that the United States had suggested some changes in dealing with Kurdish areas in the north, which have a separate allotment of food and medicine. But diplomats said no formal or informal proposal had been made by Washington.
U.S. officials would not comment on renewal of the deal.
